items.name: MCP server (122 tools) as a remote MCP server on Workers
items.detail:
apps/mcp/src/main.ts (120 lines) is a stdio client of GET /v1/tools?surface=mcp and POST /v1/tools/:name, using an mcp-scope x-api-key from WEFT_API_KEY or a key file.

The registry has 190 commands: 70 marked mcp read, 53 propose, 67 hidden. NEVER_EXPOSED filters proposals, rollback, vault, settings, api_keys, memory writes and routine toggles, leaving 121 tools, plus agent_ask: 122.

Plan:
- createMcpServer(cfg, fetchImpl) already takes a fetch, and SDK 1.32.1 ships WebStandardStreamableHTTPServerTransport (server/webStandardStreamableHttp.js). So the remote server is a stateless POST /mcp route in the front Worker: one Server and transport per request, sessionIdGenerator undefined, and fetchImpl pointed at the visitor world's DO stub.
- Auth: Authorization Bearer or x-api-key carrying the per-world mcp key minted at assignment, with a prefix that encodes the slot for routing. The DO verifies the hash.
- agent_ask polls /v1/agent/runs/:id up to 120 times at 500 ms: up to 121 subrequests, over the 50 per invocation on Free. Replace it with one long-poll endpoint that waits on the runtime's settled waiters.
- The agents SDK's McpAgent (a DO per session) is unnecessary, since the server keeps no state.
- stdio stays for local use.

items.name: Model providers through AI Gateway and Workers AI
items.detail:
**OpenAI:** openai.ts builds `new OpenAI({ apiKey, maxRetries: 0, timeout })` and calls responses.create (the Responses API, never chat completions). Add a baseURL option, https://gateway.ai.cloudflare.com/v1/<account>/<gateway>/openai, and an optional cf-aig-authorization header. The openai SDK runs on Workers. loadSecret reads OPENAI_API_KEY from env first, so a Worker secret works.

**Workers AI switch:** chat-completions.ts does a plain fetch to <base>/v1/chat/completions with live:false. Point it at the gateway's workers-ai or compat endpoint, or add a provider over env.AI.run(model, { messages, tools }, { gateway: { id } }).
- Qwen3 needs /no_think.
- Neurons (10,000 a day on Free) are not dollars, so the ledger needs a price or a separate daily cap.

**Bundle and scripts:** leave @anthropic-ai/sdk and the Claude provider out of the hosted bundle. The scripted and template providers need scenarios/*.json bundled.

items.name: Composition root, process.env and the Worker entry
items.detail:
createWeft(dataDir) wires every part and does file I/O while it builds: migrate, proxy secret, run-handle directory, vault key, world id and demo key files. Code reads process.env in many places: WEFT_LLM, WEFT_SANDBOX via sandboxFromEnv in builtins.ts, WEFT_CLOCK_RATE, WEFT_DEV_AUTH, WEFT_E2E, the cap variables, WEFT_TRACE, screeningVendor, esignEnabled.

With nodejs_compat and a recent compatibility date, process.env is filled from vars and secrets; verify this on the deploy. Passing env explicitly is safer.

Hosted entry:
- `createWeftDurable({ storage: ctx.storage, env, blobs, state, memory, ledger: spendStub, clockRate })` inside the DO constructor's blockConcurrencyWhile.
- A front Worker fetch handling routing, Turnstile, rate limits, assets and MCP.
- main.ts, scripts/dev.ts, demo.ts, testing.ts and the seed CLI stay Node-only, so tests and evals keep running on Node.
items.source: apps/api/src/compose.ts, apps/api/src/main.ts, apps/api/src/http/context.ts, packages/executor/src/builtins.ts, packages/core/src/shared/clock.ts, packages/core/src/screening/orders.ts, packages/core/src/esign/envelopes.ts

risks: Transactions are the critical path. Every one of the 33 transaction sites and all 190 command bodies are async and await drizzle (1,607 awaits in packages/core alone). The executor runs each command inside a nested savepoint. On a DO, transactionSync rejects async callbacks, sql.exec rejects BEGIN/SAVEPOINT, and ctx.storage.transaction(async) on SQLite objects has no documented rollback-on-throw or nesting. Spike this first in wrangler dev and deployed. If it fails, the fallback is a sync rewrite of the whole command layer.

Free-plan DO CPU per invocation is undocumented: the DO limits table says 30 s, the FAQ says the same as Workers (10 ms on Free). Warm routes in Node have a median of 0.5 ms, but /v1/time-off/requests takes 20 ms and /v1/time-off/balances 16 ms warm; cold isolates cost more. A tick is about 15 ms, a snapshot restore is likely hundreds of ms, and QuickJS instantiation is 20 to 29 ms. Measure cpuTime through the GraphQL Analytics API before committing; wrangler tail rarely delivers on this Mac.

Free daily rows written (100,000) versus world resets: a rich world is about 20,186 rows plus index entries per restore (base about 10,942), so at most 4 to 5 snapshot restores a day before visitor activity. PITR bookmark restore would avoid this, but it is unverified on Free, unsupported in local dev, and bookmarks expire after 30 days.

Request caps versus polling: the Worker and DO are each capped at 100,000 requests a day. The web app polls dozens of hooks at 2 to 5 s, about 1 to 3 requests per second per open tab, so the whole public demo gets roughly 10 to 30 tab-hours a day unless polling is paused when hidden or replaced by hibernatable WebSocket pushes. Always-on 5 s scheduler alarms would also burn about 17,280 requests per world per day.

The CAS invariants depend on exact rowsAffected (7 sites). DO cursors expose rowsWritten, which probably counts index entries, and proposals has two secondary indexes. A naive mapping makes every approval look already decided. The facade must use SELECT changes().
Duration budget: 13,000 GB-s a day is about 29 DO-hours at 128 MB. Open SSE streams, in-flight model waits and background runs keep objects active.

50 subrequests per invocation on Free, and whether DO RPC counts is undocumented. A 12-step chat run in one invocation (model fetch plus spend reserve/settle per attempt, plus child runs) and MCP agent_ask (up to 121 polls) can exceed it. Step runs from alarms and long-poll instead.

WEFT_LIVE_USD_CAP defaults to 0.50, cumulative over every ledger day, for live providers (openai has live:true). A public demo would exhaust it permanently. Nitish set the run cap (0.10) and day cap (2.00), but the hosted live cap needs an explicit decision.

Memory parity: the hosted SQLite MemoryStore must reproduce the git semantics tests rely on: 40-hex commit ids for SHA_RE and `at`, pinned reads, history diffs, and the Weft-Chain-Head trailer behind verifyChain gitLag. Commit ids will differ from git's, so both stores need shared contract tests.

Module-level singletons shared by DO instances in one isolate: the db write-lock tail, git's serialGit tail, otel.ts learned secrets, recallNotes keyed by run id (ids restart at run_0001 in every world), the global setTraceRedactor, and the auth Window limiters. This couples or leaks state across visitors' worlds.

Vault key fallback: without WEFT_VAULT_KEY, loadVaultKey writes run/vault.key, which on Workers lands in a per-request /tmp and mints a new key per request. Stored secrets then silently fail to decrypt (primeRedactor swallows the errors). Fail closed, and build the snapshot with the deploy key.

DO limits to enforce in the adapter: 100 bound parameters per query (the most seen in GET routes plus one tick was 72; writes and large inArray lists were not measured), 100 KB per statement, and 2 MB per row/BLOB (receipts allow 5 MB today; artifacts are unbounded JSON).

Process notes: no repo files changed. One command briefly copied a scratch script into apps/api and removed it in the same command. The static-export probe prerendered `/`, whose loadLanding() fetches 127.0.0.1:4070/v1/stats and /v1/health; Nitish's API was listening there, so two read-only GETs may have reached it (the page rendered with the fallback stats). The working tree has someone else's uncommitted edits (README.md, SPEC.md, the tour and top-bar files); this map did not touch them.
